correctness.rationale: All 2n triangular faces form n equal rhombi. Euclidean radial distance from the rhombus apex agrees on all shared upper and lower edges, so is globally continuous and piecewise gradient-1, hence 1-Lipschitz on the intrinsic surface. Each convex rhombus contains the straight radial segment from N to X, supplying the matching path and proving exact geodesic distance rather than merely a candidate upper bound. Uniform surface measure selects each rhombus equally and cancels n; n+2 curvature vertices distinguish the surfaces. Polar-coordinate integration gives F(r)=(s² sin2beta)^(-1)∫_0^beta min(r²,s² sin²2beta/sin²(beta+theta))dtheta, while independent uniform U,V coordinates give all even moments. Boundary clipping at beta=pi/4 separates quadratic and three-halves onset exponents; opposite apex gives upper quadratic tail. Reconstructed each geometric argument and independently checked selected CDF/moment/asymptotic cases; numerical checks are corroboration only.

value.rationale: Exact radial distance distributions are natural metric-measure invariants. The result constructs arbitrarily large nonisometric convex polyhedral families sharing all one-source distance quantiles, a concrete, motivated obstruction to radial inverse reconstruction, and classifies nontrivial angular threshold singularities.
